title: A Multi-Agent Deception Benchmark: When Models Deceive Other Models

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: model-to-model deception is a distinct safety problem, but the field is nascent and the practical impact depends on multi-agent deployment patterns that are still emerging.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Advanced: setting up multi-agent frameworks (LangGraph/AutoGen) with task and monitor agents, designing adversarial interactions, and categorizing deception types requires substantial infrastructure and ML knowledge.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Broad scope: designing a multi-agent benchmark from scratch, implementing two-agent interactions, running on open models, and categorizing deception types is a large project beyond 30 hours for beginners.

evidence: OpenDeception (Apr 2025) evaluates deception in multi-agent human-AI dialogue with 50 real-world scenarios across 11 LLMs and 3 large reasoning models.
'Secret Collusion among AI Agents' (arxiv 2402.07510) investigates multi-agent deception via steganography where agents deceive oversight systems.
DeceptionBench evaluates cross-model deception but in single-agent settings rather than model-to-model interactions.
The specific framing of models deceiving other models (not humans) in multi-agent task workflows is partially novel, but the broader multi-agent deception space is actively being explored.
